title: The Slow Protocol Anew
premise: Mara Sterling, a terraformer and former cargo hauler on the colony world Verdance, tends an orbital garden seeded for future generations while keeping his past buried. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream of fire in the old Hab-7 corridors, Mara recognizes it as a memory he helped erase: the Kestrel Landing massacre, officially rewritten out of every record. As the jump window to the core systems closes in ninety days, Mara must find surviving witnesses among the colonists who once trusted him, decode the garden's hidden archive, and expose the truth before the corporation's administrator purges both evidence and witnesses. In the end, Mara broadcasts the massacre record through the garden itself—sacrificing his anonymity and nearly his life—and the colonists choose to delay their own resupply rather than let the lie travel onward, forging a found family bound by shared truth.
about_author: M. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former agricultural engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction full-time. They write slow-burn science fiction about people who fix things quietly and are forced, at last, to be loud.

chapters.title: Seed Vault Lullaby
chapters.summary: Mara Sterling tends the orbital seed garden above Verdance, narrating his careful routines and deliberate invisibility. He notices the colony children below have gone quiet at recess, all staring at the sky. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment, with the first hairline crack of unease.

chapters.title: The Dream They All Share
chapters.summary: Teacher Ilsa Vann brings Mara a child's drawing: burning corridors labeled 'Hab-7,' identical to drawings from eleven other kids. None of them were alive when Hab-7 existed. Mara lies that it means nothing, then can't sleep. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: dread blooming under forced calm.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Mara hauling cargo through contested orbits, taking the terraformer job as a way to disappear after something terrible he refuses to name. Establishes his loyalty to the colony's founder, Odile Brant, who gave him sanctuary. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: guilt as a load-bearing wall.

chapters.title: Administrator Cole's Welcome
chapters.summary: Corporate administrator Dara Cole arrives ahead of the decennial jump-window resupply, charming the colonists while quietly requesting all archival access from Mara's garden systems. She mentions Hab-7 casually, watching his face. POV: alternating Mara and Cole. Emotional beat: predator and prey politely sharing tea.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Mara interviews the dreaming children; eight-year-old Tam describes a woman's voice counting down and the smell of scorched wheat—the exact details of a manifest Mara once hauled. The dreams are getting more precise nightly. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: horror sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Founder's Silence
chapters.summary: Mara confronts Odile Brant, now elderly and revered. She admits Hab-7 burned but insists no one died—that the records are simply lost. Her hands shake. Mara realizes she may be lying, or lying to herself. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking against the first hard fact of truth.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest 77-Kestrel
chapters.summary: Digging into his own twenty-year-old shipping logs, Mara finds a gap: three days erased from his personal chronometer during the Kestrel Landing incident. Someone edited him too. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the discovery that his own memory is untrustworthy terrain.

chapters.title: The Gardener Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Reclusive hydroponicist Sen Okafor admits she survived Kestrel Landing and has stayed silent for two decades to protect her daughter. She confirms forty-one deaths and names the corporate officer who ordered the corridor sealed. POV: Sen. Emotional beat: terror of testimony, relief of being believed.

chapters.title: Cole Tightens the Orbit
chapters.summary: Cole freezes off-world communications citing 'pre-jump protocol' and begins auditing colonists' data pads. Tam's family is threatened with relocation. Mara understands the purge has already started. POV: Cole, with a cold, rational interiority. Emotional beat: menace wearing a friendly uniform.

chapters.title: The Garden's Second Root System
chapters.summary: Mara discovers the seed archive contains a hidden partition built by the original terraforming crew—a dead-man's vault designed to broadcast if ever unlocked. It requires biometric keys from multiple founders. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as an engineering problem.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession, Half-Given
chapters.summary: Pressed by the children's dreams going public, Odile admits she signed the cover-up order believing she was saving the colony's charter. She refuses to give her key. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: tragic complicity—she chose the living over the dead and has regretted it ever since.

chapters.title: Night of Shared Fire
chapters.summary: Every child on the colony dreams the massacre's final minute simultaneously and wakes screaming. Parents demand answers; Cole blames a 'contaminant in the water reclamation system.' The colony splits into factions. POV: Ilsa Vann. Emotional beat: communal grief without a permitted object.

chapters.title: The Third Key
chapters.summary: Mara tracks down the third biometric holder: a dying old pilot living rough in the southern craters, who agrees to help only if Mara finally says aloud what he did during those three missing days. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: confession as the price of alliance.

chapters.title: Three Missing Days
chapters.summary: Mara's full confession: he hauled the bodies and accepted the edited manifest in exchange for his new identity. He didn't kill anyone, but he buried them twice. Sen and the pilot accept him anyway. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: shame met by found family's grace.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Seed Rings
chapters.summary: Cole's agents sabotage the garden's climate systems to force an emergency shutdown that would wipe the hidden partition. Mara and Sen run manual stabilization for thirty-six hours straight. POV: Sen. Emotional beat: exhaustion transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: The Vote Under the Dome
chapters.summary: Mara tells the assembled colonists everything. Cole counters with evidence of Mara's falsified identity, turning suspicion on him. Odile, watching her people waver, finally stands and gives her key—not for Mara, but for the dead. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: public ruin and unexpected rescue.

chapters.title: Lockout
chapters.summary: Cole seizes the garden controls and moves up the jump window, planning to leave with the archive cores aboard her ship. The vault needs four keys; they have three, and the fourth belonged to a founder long dead. POV: Cole. Emotional beat: victory curdling as she learns what the fourth key really is.

chapters.title: The Fourth Key Is a Voice
chapters.summary: Sen deciphers the vault's design: the fourth key is a spoken testimony recorded by the original crew—a witness account of Kestrel Landing, stored in the children's shared dream pattern all along. The dreams were the archive reaching for them. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: revelation reframing mystery as inheritance.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. During Cole's departure window, the colonists storm the garden, Mara unlocks the vault with the recovered testimony, and the massacre record floods every screen on-world and pings the departing ship. Cole's crew mutinies rather than carry the lie. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with exposure—he is fully seen at last.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: The colony debates what to do with delayed resupply; they vote to send the full record core to the outer systems instead of trading silence for supplies. Cole, deposed, awaits trial. The children stop dreaming the fire and begin dreaming the garden. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: grief finding its shape and setting down weight.

chapters.title: Names on the Wall
chapters.summary: The colonists build a memorial in the seed garden, engraving the forty-one names. Odile reads them aloud; Sen's daughter lays the first flower. Mara, no longer invisible, is asked to speak and manages four words. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: mourning becoming ritual, strangers becoming kin.

chapters.title: The Slow Protocol
chapters.summary: Epilogue. A year later, Mara plants the first seeds meant for the generation that will know the truth from birth. The garden's new protocol bears the massacre's date in its code so it can never be edited out again. He stays—not hiding anymore, but home. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
